text: Agreed to pace rolling endurance rides steadily on climbs without surging, using conversational breathing and comfortable cadence to control effort through the middle hours.
A final riser felt harder than usual, attributed to a headwind and a long day on the athlete’s feet rather than a negative fitness trend.
For exposed headwind sections, agreed to use a lower bar position and move snacks earlier to preserve final-hour energy, while monitoring hand and shoulder comfort as volume increases.
On the second day of back-to-back rides, mild leg heaviness cleared after 20 minutes of easy spinning; no plan adjustment was needed.
Kept the current back-to-back plan, with a rule to shorten the second ride if leg heaviness ever persists beyond 30 minutes rather than pushing through.
For rides over two hours, agreed on one bottle per hour, food every 30 minutes, and a larger breakfast before sustained climbing; the routine will be practiced on easy rides first.
The recovery route with fewer junctions allowed relaxed breathing and made genuinely easy effort easier to maintain; recovery spins will therefore start from the park side of town.
